```{r setup}

theme_update(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"))

```

## Background  

In the Bas Sassandra region of Cote d'Ivoire two hydroelectic dams were recently built:  

* [Gribo-Popoli Hydroelectric Power Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gribo%E2%80%93Popoli_Hydroelectric_Power_Station) started construction in 2018 and finished in mid 2024  
* [Soubre Hydroelectric Power Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soubr%C3%A9_Hydroelectric_Power_Station) which started construction in 2016 and finished in 2018.

This leaves 4 interesting timepoints for comparing the schistosomiasis risk in the region:  

* 2015 before any construction  
* 2017 during Soubre Dam construction / before Gribo-Popoli   
* 2019 Soubre construction complete/Gribo-Popoli under construction    
* 2025 Gribo-Popoli complete  

## Data used  

The rasters used in this analysis were downloaded using Google Earth Engine. The code for this is included in the appendix. 

```{r dams}
dam_locs <- data.frame(
  name = c("Gribo-Popoli", "Soubre"),
  lat = c(5.6980560, 5.8025358),
  lon = c(-6.5713890, -6.6558854)
) 

dam_locs <- vect(dam_locs, geom=c("lon", "lat"), crs="EPSG:4326")
dam_locs <- terra::project(dam_locs, "EPSG:32630")

dam_buffer <- buffer(hull(dam_locs, type="circle"), 
                     width = 10000)

r_names <- c("water_mask", "NDVI_dry", "NDVI_wet", "waterTemp_dry", "waterTemp_wet", "worldpop")
r_years <- c("2015", "2017", "2019", "2021", "2023", "2025") 
```

```{r damarea}
#| include: false
#| eval: false

## update dam buffer
dam_buffer_new <- as.polygons(ext(crop(r_water[[1]], dam_buffer)))
crs(dam_buffer_new) <- crs(r_water)
## crop and save the input layers so invest runs faster
cropNsave <- function(r, aoi_buffer = dam_buffer_new, yrs = r_years, 
                      folder = "G:/My Drive/De Leo Lab/projects/InVEST_schisto/CIV/Bas-Sassandra/cropped_input/cropped_"){
  rr <- crop(r, aoi_buffer)
  names(rr) <- paste(names(rr), yrs, sep="_")
  writeRaster(rr, paste0(folder, names(rr), ".tif"), overwrite=T)
}

names(r_water)
cropNsave(r=r_water)
names(r_ndvi_dry) <- rep("NDVI_dry", 6)
cropNsave(r=r_ndvi_dry)
names(r_ndvi_wet) <- rep("NDVI_wet", 6)
cropNsave(r_ndvi_wet)
names(r_temp_dry) <- rep("waterTemp_dry", 6)
cropNsave(r_temp_dry)
names(r_temp_wet) <- rep("waterTemp_wet", 6)
cropNsave(r_temp_wet)
names(r_pop)
cropNsave(r_pop, yrs=r_years[1:3])

writeVector(dam_buffer_new, "G:/My Drive/De Leo Lab/projects/InVEST_schisto/CIV/Bas-Sassandra/cropped_input/cropped_aoi.shp",
            overwrite=T)
```

### Summary  
```{r covsummary}
tmp <- cbind(
  global(r_water == 1, "sum", na.rm = TRUE),
  global(r_ndvi_dry, "mean", na.rm=TRUE),
  global(r_ndvi_wet, "mean", na.rm=TRUE),
  global(r_temp_dry, "mean", na.rm=TRUE),
  global(r_temp_wet, "mean", na.rm=TRUE)
)
tmp$sum1 <- c(global(r_pop, "sum", na.rm=TRUE)$sum, NA, NA, NA)
colnames(tmp) <- str_replace_all(paste(colnames(tmp), r_names), "_", " ")
rownames(tmp) <- r_years

tmp %>% 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~round(.x, 2))) %>%
  rownames_to_column("year") %>% 
  DT::datatable()

tmp %>% 
    rownames_to_column("year") %>% 
    mutate(year = as.integer(year)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=year, y=value)) +
    geom_point() + geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales="free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = as.integer(r_years))

## clean up workspace
```

## Risk assessments
```{r riskdat}
fl <- list.files("G:/My Drive/De Leo Lab/projects/InVEST_schisto/CIV/Bas-Sassandra/cropped_output/", full.names = T)
fl <- fl[which(str_detect(fl, "tif"))]
fl <- fl[-which(str_detect(fl, "unmasked"))]

r_risk <- rast(fl[which(str_detect(fl, "risk"))])
r_suit <- rast(fl[which(str_detect(fl, "suit"))])
```

### Risk  

The InVEST model outputs various risk estimates:  

* **convolved_hab_risk**  
* normalized_convolved_risk  
* risk_to_pop_abs  
* **risk_to_pop_count_abs**  
* risk_to_pop_count_rel  
* risk_to_pop_rel  

For the purposes of comparing between scenarios (e.g., our timepoints) the most useful outputs for comparing between scenarios are convoluted habitat risk and risk to population count absolute, as the normalized risk is normalized to within the scenario (bounded [0,1]) and [population's are relative to the total???]{style="color: red;"}, which isn't necessary since only the 2015 'baseline' populaton data was used in the model. 

::: {.panel-tabset}
```{r risk}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false

## vector of the names of all the risk estimates
nms <- names(r_risk) %>% 
  str_remove_all("_[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]") %>% 
  unique()

## subset names to just the 2 layers of interested
# nms <- nms[c(1, 3)] ## commenting out because the population doesn't make sense, the total population is 213,380

## store results
g_res <- data.frame()

## plot estimates and extract values
for (i in 1:length(nms)) {
  
  ## tab header
  cat(paste0("\n#### ", nms[i], "\n\n"))
  
  ## which r
  rr <- r_risk[[which(str_detect(names(r_risk), nms[i]))]]
  
  print(
    ggplot() +
      geom_spatraster(data=rr)+
      facet_wrap(~lyr, labeller = nice_titles)
  )
  ## mean values and sum of entire area
  g_res <- global(rr, c("sum", "mean", "sd"), na.rm = TRUE) %>% 
    rownames_to_column("var") %>% 
    rbind(g_res)
  
  ## newline
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

### Correlation between suitability and risk  
```{r}
## for risk just two trends use convolved_hab_risk, normalized_convolved_risk to rep these
gs_res <- g_res %>% 
    filter(var %in% c("convolved_hab_risk", "normalized_convolved_risk")) %>% 
    rbind(s_res) %>% 
    group_by(var) %>% 
    mutate(across(sum:sd, scale)) 

cor_long <- gs_res %>% 
    select(var, mean, year) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = var, values_from = mean)%>% 
    select(-year) %>% 
  cor() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "var1") %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -var1, 
    names_to = "var2", 
    values_to = "correlation"
  )

cor_long %>% 
    filter(str_detect(var1, "risk"),
           !str_detect(var2, "risk")
           ) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=var1, y=var2, fill=correlation)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_continuous(palette = "Reds") +
  labs(x=NULL, y=NULL)

gs_res %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=year, y=mean)) + 
    geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~var, scales="free_y", labeller = nice_titles)
```

### ESPEN data on prevalence  
```{r espen}

fp <- "G:/My Drive/De Leo Lab/projects/InVEST_schisto/schisto_waterlayers/data/"

v_epsen <- st_read(paste0(fp, "prevalence_raw/ESPEN_IU_2015.shp"))
v_epsen <- st_transform(v_epsen, crs(region_aoi))
v_epsen <- st_crop(v_epsen, region_aoi)
# plot(v_epsen)

# civ <- rgeoboundaries::gb_adm3(country = "CIV")
# civ <- st_transform(civ, crs(aoi))
# civ <- st_crop(civ, aoi)
# plot(civ)  

print(paste("The dams are in the", v_epsen$ADMIN1, "region"))

epsen_inf <- read.csv(paste0(fp, "prevalence_raw/data-CI-SCH-iu-2014-2024-20260506_161004.csv"))
epsen_inf <- epsen_inf %>% 
  filter(admin1 %in% v_epsen$ADMIN1,
         targetPop == "Total",
         year %in% as.numeric(r_years)) %>% 
  select(admin1, year, endemicity) %>% 
  mutate(endemicity = ifelse(endemicity == "Prevalence 50% and above", "High prevalence (50% and above)", endemicity),
         endemicity = factor(endemicity, levels = c("Not reported", "Non-endemic", "Low prevalence (less than 10%)",
                                                    "Moderate prevalence (10%-49%)", "High prevalence (50% and above)"))) %>% 
  group_by(admin1, year) %>% 
  slice_max(endemicity, with_ties = F) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, names_prefix = "EPSEN_", values_from = endemicity)

epsen_inf %>% 
  pivot_longer(-admin1, names_to = "Year", values_to = "Endemicity") %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = admin1, values_from = Endemicity)

## don't do this because only one region
v_epsen <- v_epsen %>%
  left_join(epsen_inf, by = c("ADMIN1" = "admin1")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("EPSEN"), names_to = "year", values_to = "value") 


ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatvector(data = v_epsen, aes(fill=value))+
  facet_wrap(~year, labeller = nice_titles) +
  geom_sf(data = aoi, fill = "transparent", col="black", lwd=1)
```
